memory_update.text: FORM should remain a high-priority underfollowed HBM test relationship: map it to memory wafer probe and known-good-die validation, then verify HBM probe-card mix, memory customer breadth, share gains, and capacity constraints.

COHU should remain a high-priority underfollowed backend test/inspection relationship: map it to HBM inspection, metrology, contactors, handlers, and AI/HPC thermal test, then verify repeat HBM orders and revenue materiality.

ALAB is best treated as a reference anchor rather than discovery alpha: map it to AI fabric interconnect and PCIe/CXL connectivity silicon, with evidence work focused on concentration, content per cluster, competition, and insourcing risk.

AIXA.DE is an underfollowed upstream optics tools candidate: map it to compound-semiconductor epitaxy equipment for InP/GaAs lasers and photonics, but require order/backlog proof tied specifically to AI optical demand.

AXTI is a speculative-shadow InP substrate candidate: the bottleneck thesis depends on CPO/optical interconnect adoption, actual InP revenue mix, qualification at laser/photonics customers, and proof that concentrated supply creates pricing power.
ONTO maps to advanced packaging inspection/metrology and process control; verify whether AI/HBM/panel-level packaging revenue is large enough to offset broader semiconductor cyclicality.

AMKR is a reference OSAT capacity anchor for advanced packaging and test; keep it in the map but do not upgrade without evidence of direct AI accelerator, HBM-adjacent, 2.5D, fan-out, or interposer work.
KLIC remains a hypothesis around thermocompression bonding and advanced packaging assembly equipment; verify mix shift away from legacy wire bonding and actual HBM/chiplet-related system shipments.

PTI.TW maps to memory backend outsourcing and FOPLP advanced packaging; external context is supportive but primary-source confirmation is required for AMD/Broadcom validation, 90% pilot yield, price increases, and revenue conversion.

Layer 2B still needs primary-source filing checks for all candidates, especially customer concentration, AI/HBM/CPO revenue materiality, backlog conversion, utilization, pricing power, and whether demand is incremental versus cyclical recovery.

Market-pricing checks are still missing for the chunk: current market capitalization, valuation, estimate revisions, short interest, liquidity, and analyst coverage should be collected before Layer 2C or ranking upgrades.

summary: Layer 2B maps the candidate chunk into ticker-to-node relationships across AI infrastructure supply-chain chokepoints. The strongest relationship cluster is HBM/advanced-packaging test and inspection, led by FormFactor, Cohu, Onto Innovation, Amkor, Kulicke & Soffa, and Powertech. A second cluster covers AI fabric and optical/compound-semiconductor bottlenecks, with Astera Labs as the reference anchor and Aixtron/AXT as upstream discovery or speculative-shadow names. Evidence is strongest where company exposure is already explicit in the Layer 1 cache or external search context; evidence remains weaker for exact customer mix, revenue materiality, and whether AI/HBM/CPO demand is incremental rather than a cyclical semi rebound.
